record.original_question: Let ψ : S 1 → S 1 be a homeomorphism. When is it true that Re A = Re A ◦ ψ? That is, when is each function f in the real part of the disc algebra also of the form g ◦ ψ, for some function g in the disc algebra? O’Connell [609] has shown that it is necessary that ψ is absolutely continuous, and sufficient that ψ is C 1+ε . (A. G. O’Farrell)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S^1$ denote the unit circle in $\mathbb{C}$, and let $A$ denote the disc algebra, i.e., the algebra of continuous functions $f : \overline{\mathbb{D}} \to \mathbb{C}$ on the closed unit disc $\overline{\mathbb{D}} = \{z \in \mathbb{C} : |z| \le 1\}$ that are holomorphic on the open disc $\mathbb{D}$. Identify each $f \in A$ with its restriction to $S^1$, and let $\operatorname{Re} A = \{\operatorname{Re} f|_{S^1} : f \in A\}$ denote the real part of the disc algebra, viewed as a space of real-valued continuous functions on $S^1$.

Given a homeomorphism $\psi : S^1 \to S^1$, define $\operatorname{Re} A \circ \psi = \{u \circ \psi : u \in \operatorname{Re} A\}$.

Problem. Characterize, in terms of the regularity of $\psi$, those homeomorphisms $\psi : S^1 \to S^1$ for which
$$\operatorname{Re} A = \operatorname{Re} A \circ \psi,$$
that is, those $\psi$ such that for every $f \in A$ there exists $g \in A$ with $\operatorname{Re} f = \operatorname{Re} g \circ \psi$ on $S^1$.

It is known that this equality forces $\psi$ to be absolutely continuous, and that $\psi \in C^{1+\varepsilon}$ (for some $\varepsilon > 0$) is sufficient. The problem is to determine the precise regularity condition on $\psi$ characterizing this equality.
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface a definitive characterization closing the gap between the necessary condition (absolute continuity of $\psi$) and the sufficient condition ($\psi \in C^{1+\varepsilon}$). No published resolution of the precise regularity threshold was found, so the status is recorded as unknown.

status_evidence.title: Characterizations of circle homeomorphisms of different regularities
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses regularity classes of circle homeomorphisms (quasisymmetric, symmetric, C^{1+alpha}) but does not address the Re A = Re A o psi problem.
status_evidence.claim: Related literature on circle homeomorphism regularity does not provide a characterization for the disc-algebra equation in question.
